problem: On-policy VLN training (scheduled sampling, DAgger) lets the agent explore, but once it deviates from the expert path the original instruction no longer describes the executed visual stream, so exploratory trajectories lack semantically aligned language supervision.
motivation: On-policy exploration broadens the state distribution and is important for robust VLN, but most rollouts only get action corrections under a mismatched instruction. Relabeling the agent's own journey in hindsight with an LVLM could turn these rollouts into dense, language-grounded training data and cut dependence on costly expert demonstrations.
key_idea: Wrap existing on-policy VLN training in a three-stage cycle: sample an oracle-guided rollout, have a zero-shot LVLM speaker write a path-level hindsight instruction with an expert-in-context example, then imitate the agent's own actions under that instruction, weighted by a CLIP-based trajectory-instruction alignment score.
insight: Hindsight instructions give real gains on top of standard on-policy training (ETPNav R2R-CE val-unseen SR 57.21 to 62.58). Ablations show that the noise control matters. Adaptive alignment weighting beats fixed lambda (SR 62.58 vs 59.12 at 0.1 and 58.58 at 1.0), and landmark-aware scoring beats generic scoring (62.58 vs 61.18). Expert-in-context prompting yields more train-distribution-like text than zero-shot (SPL 52.74 vs 50.55) and than template prompting. A 3B speaker is clearly worse (SR 58.11), so speaker quality matters.
method: Stage 1 On-policy sampling: standard scheduled sampling or DAgger rollout with mixed expert/agent actions, supervised by cross-entropy on expert actions under the original instruction (L_expert).

Hindsight Speaker Agent: zero-shot Qwen2.5-VL-7B takes the on-policy trajectory video (monocular frames subsampled every 2 steps, or 4-view panoramas per step) and writes a path-level instruction, so it can describe detours.

Expert-in-context learning: one sampled expert trajectory-instruction pair is placed in the prompt, with constraints on grounding, style, flow, termination and forbidden words, to match the human instruction distribution.

Trajectory-instruction alignment weighting (TIAW): lambda is the mean of a coarse CLIP video-sentence cosine score and a fine score. The fine score is the harmonic mean of bidirectional frame-landmark alignments, with landmark nouns extracted by spaCy.
Stage 3 Hindsight imitation: a second pass maximizes the likelihood of the agent's executed actions under I_H, with total loss L = L_expert + lambda * L_hindsight.
Integration: for DAgger (CMA), hindsight pairs go into the same buffer; for ETPNav, the three-stage cycle runs per sampled trajectory.

setting.backbone: Policies: CMA (monocular, DAgger) and ETPNav (panoramic, topological map, scheduled sampling), both trained. Hindsight speaker: Qwen2.5-VL-7B (frozen, zero-shot); CLIP used for alignment scoring.
setting.training_data: R2R-CE and RxR-CE expert demonstrations plus on-policy self-generated hindsight instruction-trajectory pairs; no extra external data.
setting.observation: Monocular RGB (CMA) or panoramic RGB (ETPNav, plus the baselines' depth/waypoint setup); the speaker only sees RGB frames
setting.action_space: Low-level FORWARD/TURN LEFT/TURN RIGHT/STOP for CMA; topological waypoint actions for ETPNav
setting.privileged: Expert oracle actions and expert demonstrations at training time only; none at test time

numbers.extra: scheduled sampling; hindsight speaker used in training only

numbers_note: Test-unseen results are unavailable because the VLN-CE evaluation server was deprecated. The sample-efficiency results are given only in figures, not tables.
results: Φ-Nav consistently improves on-policy baselines. ETPNav on R2R-CE val-unseen goes from SR 57.21 / SPL 49.15 to 62.58 / 52.74, slightly above g3D-LF (61 / 52). CMA-D-P-A gains +1.98 SR. On RxR-CE val-unseen ETPNav gains about +1.04 SR and +1.06 SPL, and the paper reports surpassing the baseline's best result with only 90% of the expert data.
limitations: Hindsight instructions from the LVLM remain imperfect, and gains are smaller on long-horizon RxR-CE, where fine-grained instruction generation is harder.
The alignment weight is a lightweight CLIP-based heuristic; it lacks reference-free scoring and adds LVLM inference overhead to training.
Test-unseen results are missing, and evaluation covers only two policies, with no real-robot experiments.
